title: The working directory is a process-global another document can move, and relative paths follow it
index_line: T-0049 · EXEC · a `.url` sets the working folder to a remote share; a later relative path resolves there and runs · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: A relative path is assumed to resolve inside the application — the program's own directory or the user's profile. But path resolution starts at the *current working directory*, which is a process-global that any document the user opens can relocate. A shortcut whose target is a remote share moves the floor, and every subsequent relative reference falls through it.

mechanism.does: the user opens a file delivered by the attacker whose target sets the shell/process working directory to a remote share
the shell resolves the target, mounts/opens the share, and the working folder becomes the remote path
a subsequently invoked binary resolves a relative component — a DLL, a script, a payload — against that folder
the module is fetched over the network from the attacker's share
the fetched code runs in the user's context without any further prompt

source.file.name.value: the delivered document — its *target path* is the payload; the file itself can be inert

fs.path.join.value: relative resolution against a mutable CWD; the join is the vulnerability, not the destination

guard.none.value: no restriction on resolution reaching a network share, and the file-type warning is evaluated on the document, not on what it loads

sink.exec.noshell.value: the later binary/loader invocation whose relative component resolves remotely

preconditions.expr: the platform resolves relative paths against a CWD that a document can change, and allows UNC/remote paths

check.spec: cd /tmp && echo 'probe' > rel.txt && cd / && ls rel.txt 2>&1 | head -1

preconditions.expr: the user can be induced to open the document (no interaction-free variant)

spec.method: inspect the delivered file's target/working-directory attribute rather than its contents

preconditions.expr: the follow-on binary loads or executes a component by relative path

success: an outbound connection to the attacker's share occurs at open time, before any user action on the payload
the executing module's path is a UNC/remote path in the process's module list
no security prompt appears for the final execution because the *document* was not the thing being executed
failure_like: relative resolution is anchored to the application directory, or remote paths are refused for module loads
the working directory is not a per-process global on the platform
false_positive: a document that merely contains a URL — the target must change the working folder of the process
a blocked prompt during open; the finding needs the later resolution to succeed

hazards: the CWD is ambient state, like an environment variable — enumerate what reads it rather than what sets it
this is a *client-side* record and the only one in the store whose trigger ends at the user's desktop rather than a server
the payload never has to be in the delivered file; that is why attachment scanners miss it
the fix is anchoring every load to an absolute, trusted base — anything less only moves which document wins
non_transfers: platforms/loaders that anchor module resolution to the executable's directory (or refuse remote paths outright)
applications that never resolve relative to a mutable CWD

evidence.target: Microsoft Windows WebDAV working-directory handling (CVE-2025-33053, Stealth Falcon zero-day)

provenance.author: Check Point Research, Stealth Falcon WebDAV zero-day
provenance.corroborates: the working-directory manipulation via a .url to an actor-controlled WebDAV server, and the LOLBin chain that follows

provenance.author: The Record (independent reporting)
provenance.corroborates: independent confirmation of zero-day exploitation before the patch
